description: Join our friendly and dedicated GP surgery team as a Reception and Administrator and play a vital role in providing an excellent service to our patients and supporting the smooth running of the practice. We are looking for a professional, approachable and organised individual who enjoys working with people and can remain calm and efficient in a busy environment. You will be one of the first points of contact for our patients, providing a welcoming, helpful and confidential service. The role offers variety and includes handling patient reception calls and registration, appointment administration, processing and managing referrals, patient recalls, dealing with patient enquiries, maintaining accurate medical records, scanning and coding clinical correspondence, and supporting the wider clinical and administrative teams . You will need excellent communication and organisational skills, attention to detail and a strong understanding of confidentiality and the importance of handling sensitive patient information appropriately. Previous experience in a GP surgery or NHS setting would be desirable. In return, you will join a supportive and collaborative team where your contribution genuinely matters. You will have the opportunity to develop your skills within primary care and make a positive difference to patients and the local community every day. If you are caring, reliable, organised and committed to providing high-quality patient care and service , we would love to hear from you. The successful candidate will provide a professional, friendly and efficient reception and administrative service to patients and the wider practice team. Main duties will include: Welcoming and assisting patients in person, by telephone and through online services. Managing appointments, queries and general patient enquiries. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient information. Processing and monitoring referrals, ensuring relevant information is recorded and followed up appropriately. Maintaining, updating and managing electronic and paper medical records. Scanning, coding and processing incoming clinical correspondence and documents. Carrying out patient recalls and supporting the practice with routine health checks, reviews and other recall programmes. Liaising with patients, GPs, nurses, hospitals and other healthcare professionals when required. Handling confidential and sensitive information in accordance with practice policies and data protection requirements. Supporting the clinical and administrative teams with the smooth day-to-day running of the surgery. Providing a high standard of patient service while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality and accuracy at all times. Job Title: GP Surgery ReceptionistJob Purpose To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, GPs, nurses and the wider practice team. The receptionist will act as an important first point of contact for patients and help ensure the smooth and effective running of the surgery. Welcome patients and visitors to the practice in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Answer telephone calls promptly and deal with patient enquiries appropriately and sensitively. Book, cancel and rearrange appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Register new patients and ensure registration information is accurate and up to date. Direct patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or service while maintaining confidentiality. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence and administrative documentation. Assist with opening and closing procedures and maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception area. Desirable: Previous experience working in a GP surgery, NHS or healthcare environment. Knowledge of GP practice systems and NHS primary care processes. Experience of patient registration, referrals, medical records and recall systems. We are looking for someone who is compassionate, organised, reliable, professional and confident , with a genuine commitment to providing excellent patient service and supporting colleagues.

title: Referrals Out Administrator
description: Referrals Out Administrators are an integral part of the Outpatients team, processing the onward referrals for patients who have been referred elsewhere for diagnostics or procedures. The key responsibilities are ensuring that referrals are sent within the expected timeframes, with all required information included, and actively monitoring the flow of information throughout the patient pathway. Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and the successful candidate must have existing right to work in the UK. We screen and shortlist suitable candidates as applications are received. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and without notice if we fill the position. Therefore, we encourage early applications to avoid disappointment. Organisation, prioritisation, IT skills, and attention to detail will be crucial in this role as you will be responsible for sending urgent and routine referrals to other providers and ensuring they have all the information needed to continue the patient's care. You will need to gather all the relevant information from different areas of the patient record system, including booking forms, clinic letters, BMI and blood results, and chase up any missing information with the clinicians or patients. Full training will be given on how to use our patient record system and complete the role. JOB SUMMARY The role (and team) is an integral part of the patient pathway. You will undertake tasks essential to the smooth and effective provision of quality care, providing an efficient level of service for patients and their families. The role will work within the priorities and expectations set out by the Lead Referrals-Out Administrator. It is essential the post holder displays organisation, prioritisation, IT skills and attention to detail will be crucial in this role as you will be creating referrals on patient records to other providers. You will need to gather all the relevant information from the patient record system, submit it via email to the provider & update the patient record. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE POST Referral Processing Process outbound referrals for diagnostics and procedures in line with clinical instructions and referral pathways. Ensure all referrals are correctly triaged, recorded, and actioned within agreed timeframes. Liaise with clinical teams and patients to clarify referral details or gather additional information as needed. Upload or send referrals via appropriate systems (e-RS, email, secure portals). Coordination & Communication Communicate clearly and professionally with external providers (e.g., hospitals, imaging centres, specialist clinics) to confirm referral receipt and appointment arrangements. Respond to incoming queries from patients, clinicians, and third parties regarding referrals, providing updates or advice as appropriate. Monitor referral progress and follow up to ensure timely outcomes or to troubleshoot delays. Managing multiple tasks, prioritising own workload, and ensuring work is completed within target timeframes for processing routine and urgent referrals. Work closely with the wider DHC administration and clinical teams to support seamless patient journeys. Pathway Knowledge & Relationship Management Ensure knowledge and understanding of patient pathways is maintained, including referral routes and any associated criteria for trust hospitals and independent providers. Develop and maintain relationships with other providers we work closely with. Sourcing new referral pathways, ensuring referral forms are updated, and the contact address database is maintained accurately. Contribute to maintaining and updating referral protocols and standard operating procedures. Data Management & Reporting Accurately input and update referral information in clinical systems to support timely patient care. Keep thorough documentation and audit trails in line with data protection and confidentiality policies. Contribute to performance monitoring through accurate data capture and referral tracking insights. General Undertake any other reasonable duties as commensurate with the nature of this role. Maintain mandatory training compliance. WORK SETTING AND REVIEW To manage own workload efficiently and effectively on a daily basis. Maintain confidentiality at all times. Acting independently but, where necessary, referring problems to the Referrals-Out Team Leader or the appropriate consultant via the quickest route possible. CONFIDENTIALITY The post holder must maintain the confidentiality of information about patients, staff, and DHC business in accordance with the Data Protection Act 1998 and the Caldicott principles.

The standard working pattern for this role is Monday to Friday, 12:00pm to 8:00pm . SPA clinicians work 12-hour shift patterns over 3 days working Monday Friday 07:45 20:15. Processing referrals through the SPA pathway using SystmOne, ensuring accurate data entry and record management. Arranging and booking assessments with SPA practitioners and supporting the coordination of appointments. Supporting the onward referral of triaged and assessed service users to appropriate Trust services and external agencies. Preparing and distributing correspondence, including discharge letters and outcome communications following triage, assessment and multidisciplinary team discussions. title: Pharmacy Administrator
description: The successful applicant will support a wide range of pharmacy workflows including prescription administration, patient recall programmes and long-term condition clinics. You will act as a key point of contact for patients, community pharmacies and external organisations enquiring about prescriptions. This role brings the opportunity to assist in co-ordinating medication reviews, support audit programmes and manage patient recall systems. To thrive in this role, you will enjoy working in a fast-paced environment with multiple competing priorities. You will possess excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively with patients and healthcare professionals. You will be committed to delivering excellent patient care and able to work both independently and as part of a team. The successful candidate will demonstrate a professional, flexible, and friendly manner. As well as being organised, applicants should have strong IT skills with experience of working with confidential information. Experience of EMIS web and a good understanding of medical terminology is advantageous. As a training practice, we offer a supportive environment with opportunities for learning and development within a growing multidisciplinary pharmacy team. Responsibilities The following are the core responsibilities of the Pharmacy team administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels. Prescription administration and medicines management Patient recall and service coordination Administration for medicines optimisation and clinical pharmacy support Audit, quality improvement and safety Training and team support Process repeat prescription requests received by phone, email, post, slips and the online access system, in accordance with practice protocol and standard operating procedures. Generate requests for non-repeat medications on behalf of patients, obtaining additional information where required. Manage and coordinate weekly prescription workflows to ensure timely processing of prescriptions. Ensure prescription requests are processed within agreed timescales. Escalate urgent prescription requests to the Clinical Pharmacy Team or duty GP as appropriate. Support electronic Repeat Dispensing (eRD) initiatives and encourage suitable patients to use eRD and synchronised medication collections Actively encourage patients to reconcile medications to facilitate monthly collections and electronic repeat dispensing. Act upon prescription compliance issues, liaising with the appropriate clinician. Have oversight of community pharmacy emergency supplies, escalating to the clinical pharmacy team when necessary. Build good working relationships with local Pharmacies to help enable our prescription service. Check emails regularly and deal with them appropriately. Patient recall and service coordination: Maintain medication review recall systems and invite patients for reviews in line with practice procedures. Manage medication review recall lists, including sending invitations, booking appointments and following up non-responders. Liaise with the Pharmacy Technician team regarding any monitoring requirements prior to medication reviews and arrange appointments or investigations as directed. Coordinate recalls for annual medication reviews, long-term condition reviews and pharmacist-led clinics. Book, rearrange and manage appointments for pharmacy-led services. Coordinate spirometry appointments and six-monthly heart failure recall programmes. Support the administration and management of the practice blood pressure monitor loan scheme. Maintain accurate records of recalls, appointments and patient communications. Medicines optimisation and clinical pharmacy support: Process administrative correspondence relating to weight management services, contraception services, Pharmacy First referrals and provision of cannabis therapy letters. Add medication information and relevant coding to patient records in accordance with practice protocols and escalate any clinical concerns or treatment decisions to the Pharmacy Technician or Clinical Pharmacist team. Liaise with Pharmacy Technicians regarding monitoring requirements before medication reviews. Assist with the preparation and booking of Structured Medication Reviews. Process non-complex medication-related correspondence in accordance with practice protocols. Liaise with pharmacies on the supply of prescribed drugs, alert our clinicians of any supply issues and forward information on the recommended alternative. Respond to enquiries from patients, carers, secretaries, NHS administrators, Consultants or the Medicines Management Team in a courteous, timely and efficient manner, by telephone, letter and email, occasionally face-to-face and maintain precise records of the communications. Support administration of long-term condition clinics and medicines optimisation programmes. Support delivery of medicines optimisation audits and quality improvement projects. Coordinate and support CQC, PQS, internal practice audits and high-risk drug monitoring. Undertake monthly medication ordering audits and reception medication request audits. Assist with data collection, reporting and maintenance of audit trackers. Support the administrative management of MHRA alerts, medication recalls and prescribing safety initiatives. Run searches and reports as requested and maintain accurate records of completed actions. Support the Clinical Pharmacy Team in reviewing and updating the practice prescribing related policies. Support the training of reception and administrative staff in prescription processes, prescribing workflows and pharmacy-related procedures. Contribute to improving pharmacy administrative processes and service delivery. Work collaboratively with Clinical Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians and the wider practice team to support effective patient care. This Job Description is neither exhaustive nor exclusive and will be reviewed periodically in conjunction with the post holder. description: We are looking for an organised, proactive and customer-focused Operational Support Administrator to join the Operational Support Team at East Midlands Ambulance Service NHS Trust. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and takes pride in delivering a high-quality support service. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the administration of the Trust's fleet and operational support functions, ensuring that records, systems and documentation are maintained accurately and efficiently. Working closely with colleagues across the Trust, Finance teams, suppliers and external stakeholders, you will help ensure that operational support processes run smoothly and effectively. This role requires excellent attention to detail, strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities whilst maintaining high standards of customer service The Operational Support Administrator will provide comprehensive administrative support to the Operational Support Team, ensuring that information is processed accurately and within required timescales. You will be responsible for maintaining fleet-related records and supporting the administration of vehicle maintenance, compliance and operational processes across the Trust. Key responsibilities include processing purchase invoices and fleet system transactions, maintaining vehicle records, supporting fuel card administration, producing reports, managing correspondence and acting as the first point of contact for enquiries. The post holder will also assist with insurance claim administration, audit preparation, document management and the creation of accurate management information to support operational decision-making. You will work collaboratively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders, ensuring a professional, responsive and customer-focused service is delivered at all times. The Operational Support Administrator will provide effective and efficient administrative support to the Operational Support Team in line with Trust policies and procedures. Responsibilities will include maintaining accurate fleet and vehicle records, processing invoices and financial documentation, administering sales orders and job cards through fleet management systems, and ensuring all information is recorded and maintained to a high standard. They will liaise with Finance colleagues, suppliers and operational teams to resolve queries promptly and ensure accurate financial processing. The successful candidate will act as the first point of contact for the department, providing a professional service when handling telephone calls, visitors and correspondence. They will prepare meeting minutes, produce and distribute routine and ad hoc reports, and support the gathering and collation of information for audits and performance monitoring activities. Candidates should have significant administrative experience, strong IT skills, excellent organisational abilities and the confidence to work both independently and as part of a team. The ability to prioritise workload, meet deadlines, communicate effectively and maintain a high level of accuracy is essential. Experience of working within a fleet, transport, automotive or similarly regulated environment would be advantageous

title: Senior Receptionist
description: Working pattern: Full-time. Part-time would be considered. Job Location : Dorking Hospital, with travel and work across other DHC Outpatient sites. As a Senior Receptionist, you will play a key role in supporting the smooth running of reception services across DHC Outpatient locations. Working closely with the Lead Receptionist, you will help coordinate the day-to-day work of the reception team, support staff, assist with rota planning and act as a point of escalation for more complex patient enquiries or issues. The role combines hands-on reception duties with team support and operational coordination, helping to ensure patients, clinicians, and colleagues receive a professional, efficient, and compassionate service. We are looking for someone who is organised, proactive, reliable, and patient-focused. You will need excellent communication skills, strong administrative ability and the confidence to manage competing priorities in a busy outpatient environment. The successful candidate will be someone who takes ownership of tasks, works well under pressure, supports colleagues, maintains confidentiality, and is committed to improving the experience of patients and the wider team. We screen and shortlist suitable candidates as applications are received. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and without notice if we fill the position. Therefore, we encourage early applications to avoid disappointment. This is an excellent opportunity to join DHC Outpatients as part of an independent NHS organisation that values high standards, teamwork, and continuous improvement. You will be joining a service where your contribution can make a real difference to patients and colleagues every day, helping clinics run effectively, supporting the reception team, and playing an important part in delivering responsive, patient-centred outpatient care. As Senior Receptionist, you will help coordinate reception services across DHC Outpatient locations, ensuring patients receive a professional, efficient and welcoming service. Working with the Lead Receptionist, you will support team supervision, rota planning, training, service standards and escalation of complex patient enquiries. You will also help investigate incidents, monitor performance and fill vacant clinic appointments to maximise capacity and reduce waiting times. This role combines reception duties with leadership and operational support. We are looking for an organised, proactive and patient-focused individual with good communication, administration and IT skills. You will be confident in a busy environment, able to manage competing priorities, support colleagues, solve problems and maintain confidentiality. Attention to detail, a positive attitude, and a commitment to continuous improvement are essential. Training will be provided for our in-house IT systems; however good working knowledge of Microsoft Office is beneficial. Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and the successful candidate must have an existing right to work in the UK. JOB SUMMARY The Senior Receptionist is responsible for supporting the Lead Receptionist in the day-to-day management and coordination of reception services across all DHC outpatient locations. Acting as deputy to the Lead Receptionist, the post holder will provide operational leadership to the reception team, ensuring high standards of patient service, administrative efficiency, and compliance with departmental procedures. The role combines hands-on reception duties with supervisory responsibilities, including staff support, rota coordination, training, performance monitoring, and ensuring reception functions are delivered effectively and consistently. The Senior Receptionist will act as the first point of escalation for more complex patient enquiries and service issues, exercising initiative, judgement, confidentiality, and diplomacy when resolving concerns. In the absence of the Lead Receptionist, the Senior Receptionist will oversee reception operations, allocate workloads, monitor performance indicators, and ensure appropriate staffing levels are maintained to support the smooth and effective delivery of outpatient services. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE POST Support the Lead Receptionist in the day-to-day supervision and coordination of the reception team. Act as deputy for the Lead Receptionist during periods of absence, annual leave, or when off-site. Allocate daily responsibilities and monitor workload distribution to ensure efficient service delivery. Provide guidance, support, and coaching to reception staff to promote high performance and development. Assist with recruitment, induction, training, and competency assessments for new and existing team members. Support the completion of probation reviews, one-to-one meetings, appraisals, and development plans. Monitor staff attendance, punctuality, and compliance with departmental procedures, escalating concerns where appropriate. Assist in identifying training needs and opportunities for professional development. Produce and maintain team rotas, ensuring adequate staffing levels and reception cover across all DHC locations. Investigate incidents and record findings on the incident reporting platform. Coordinate adjustments to rotas to accommodate annual leave, sickness absence, training, and service requirements. Monitor reception performance against departmental KPIs and support improvement initiatives where required. Support the Lead Receptionist in reviewing patient feedback, complaints, and service performance metrics. Proactively contact patients to fill vacant clinic appointments, utilising waiting lists and cancellation lists to maximise clinic capacity and minimise unused appointment slots. Ensure reception processes comply with organisational policies, information governance requirements, and local procedures. Where required, act as a receptionist, which consists of: Being first point of contact for clinicians, staff, patients, carers, and service providers. Management of appointment bookings, cancellations, and rescheduling. Handling escalated patient concerns and complex enquiries. Maintaining accurate patient records. Answering incoming calls and responding to requests for information. Processing departmental mail. Attending relevant meetings and training sessions. Undertaking any other duties appropriate to the grade and nature of the role. WORK SETTING AND REVIEW To manage own workload efficiently and effectively on a daily basis. Maintain confidentiality at all times. Make decisions pertaining to the smooth and efficient running of DHC Operations, where necessary referring problems to senior management via the quickest route possible. Be able to work with a degree of autonomy . Work with a continuous improvement mindset. Work to objectives as set by the DHC Board of Directors. CONFIDENTIALITY The post holder must maintain the confidentiality of information about patients, staff and DHC business in accordance with the Data Protection Act 1998 and Caldicott principles.
